questions.prompt: Why does lactic acid build-up occur during sprinting?
options: Muscles switch to anaerobic glycolysis when oxygen delivery lags demand
Sweat glands release acid into the bloodstream
The heart pumps blood away from muscles during effort
Lungs stop absorbing oxygen at high speeds
questions.explanation: Sprinting demands ATP faster than aerobic metabolism can supply it, so muscles use anaerobic glycolysis, whose by-product (lactate + H+) accumulates and produces the classic burning sensation.

micro_lesson.title: Energy Systems 101
micro_lesson.body: Your body has three fuel pathways: ATP-PC (0-10s bursts), anaerobic glycolysis (10s-2min, produces lactate), and aerobic metabolism (sustained efforts). Sprints outrun the aerobic system's delivery rate.
micro_lesson.takeaway: The burn is a fuel-supply gap, not damage — pacing and conditioning widen the gap you can tolerate.

questions.prompt: Why do basketball players jump higher after a running approach than from standing?
options: The approach stores elastic energy and pre-loads the stretch-shortening cycle
Air resistance is lower when moving
Gravity briefly weakens for moving bodies
questions.explanation: A running approach lets tendons and muscles pre-stretch (eccentric load); the stretch-shortening cycle then releases stored elastic energy on top of concentric muscle force, adding centimeters to the jump.

micro_lesson.title: The Stretch-Shortening Cycle
micro_lesson.body: Muscles and tendons behave like springs: a rapid pre-stretch followed by immediate contraction produces more force than contraction alone. Plyometric training targets exactly this cycle.
micro_lesson.takeaway: Train the spring, not just the motor — plyometrics convert speed into height.

questions.prompt: Why is the sky blue during the day but red at sunset?
options: Shorter blue wavelengths scatter more; at sunset light crosses more atmosphere, leaving red
The sun changes color through the day
Clouds filter out blue at dusk
questions.explanation: Rayleigh scattering disperses short (blue) wavelengths most. At sunset, light travels a longer path through the atmosphere, scattering blue away entirely and leaving the longer red wavelengths.

micro_lesson.title: Rayleigh Scattering
micro_lesson.body: Scattering intensity scales with 1/wavelength^4, so blue light scatters roughly 5x more than red. Path length through the atmosphere decides which wavelengths survive to your eye.
micro_lesson.takeaway: Same sunlight, different path length — geometry paints the sky.

questions.prompt: Why does compound interest grow savings faster than simple interest?
options: Each period's interest is added to the principal and itself earns interest
Banks pay higher base rates for compound accounts
Simple interest stops after ten years
questions.explanation: Compound interest is exponential: interest earned is reinvested, so the base grows every period. Simple interest stays linear on the original principal.

micro_lesson.title: Exponential vs Linear Growth
micro_lesson.body: At 7% compounded annually, money doubles in about 10 years (Rule of 72: 72 / rate = doubling time). Time in the market beats timing the market because the exponent is time.
micro_lesson.takeaway: Start early: the exponent — time — is the most powerful variable you control.

questions.prompt: Why can you feel sore two days AFTER a hard workout rather than immediately?
options: Micro-tears trigger an inflammatory repair response that peaks 24-72h later
Lactic acid stays trapped in the muscle for two days
The nervous system delays all pain by 48 hours
questions.explanation: Delayed-onset muscle soreness (DOMS) comes from the inflammatory phase of repairing exercise-induced micro-damage — not lactate, which clears within an hour. The repair cascade peaks one to three days post-exercise.

micro_lesson.title: DOMS and Adaptation
micro_lesson.body: Eccentric (lengthening) contractions cause the most micro-damage and the most soreness — but also drive adaptation. Repeated-bout effect: the same workout hurts less the second time.
micro_lesson.takeaway: Soreness is the repair bill, not the receipt for progress — track load, not pain.

questions.prompt: Why do international flights heading east often arrive faster than the return leg?
options: Jet streams — high-altitude westerly winds — boost eastbound groundspeed
Airlines use faster planes going east
questions.explanation: Jet streams are narrow bands of strong westerly wind at cruise altitude. Flying east rides the tailwind; flying west fights a headwind, so the same route differs by an hour or more.

micro_lesson.title: Jet Streams
micro_lesson.body: Jet streams form where cold and warm air masses meet, flowing west-to-east at 100-200 km/h. Pilots route into them eastbound and around them westbound.
micro_lesson.takeaway: The atmosphere has highways — riding them beats fighting them.

questions.prompt: Why does a curveball actually curve?
options: Spin creates a pressure differential across the ball (Magnus effect)
The seams make the ball heavier on one side
questions.explanation: A spinning ball drags air around itself; air moves faster on one side and slower on the other, creating a pressure difference that pushes the ball sideways — the Magnus effect.

micro_lesson.title: The Magnus Effect
micro_lesson.body: Topspin dives, backspin floats, sidespin curves. The same physics powers soccer free kicks, tennis topspin, and golf slices.
micro_lesson.takeaway: Spin is steering — control the axis and you control the flight.

questions.prompt: Why is sleep considered a performance enhancer for athletes?
options: Growth hormone release, memory consolidation, and tissue repair concentrate during sleep
Sleep burns more calories than training
Muscles only grow when the brain is off
questions.explanation: Deep sleep drives the largest natural growth-hormone pulse of the day, motor learning consolidates during REM, and reaction time degrades measurably with sleep debt — sleep is when training becomes adaptation.

micro_lesson.title: Sleep as Training
micro_lesson.body: Studies on basketball players extending sleep to 10h showed faster sprints and +9% free-throw accuracy. Reaction time after 20h awake resembles legal intoxication.
micro_lesson.takeaway: You don't get stronger in the gym — you get stronger in bed. Protect the hours.

questions.prompt: Why does the moon show phases?
options: We see varying fractions of its sunlit half as it orbits Earth
Earth's shadow covers part of the moon each night
Clouds on the moon block reflected light
The moon emits light that fades monthly
questions.explanation: Half the moon is always sunlit. As the moon orbits Earth over ~29.5 days, we view that lit half from changing angles — from none (new) to all (full). Earth's shadow is only involved in eclipses, not phases.

micro_lesson.title: Phases vs Eclipses
micro_lesson.body: Phases are geometry: sun-moon-Earth angles. A lunar eclipse (Earth's shadow on the moon) needs perfect alignment and is rare; phases repeat monthly.
micro_lesson.takeaway: The moon never changes — your viewing angle does.

questions.prompt: Why do muscles shake during a maximal-effort lift?
options: Motor units fire asynchronously as the nervous system recruits near its limit
Blood sugar crashes instantly under load
Oxygen is cut off to the arms
questions.explanation: Near maximal effort, the nervous system recruits nearly all motor units at high firing rates. Their activation is imperfectly synchronized, and fatigue makes firing irregular — visible as shaking.

micro_lesson.title: Motor Unit Recruitment
micro_lesson.body: Strength gains in the first weeks of training are mostly neural: the brain learns to recruit more units, faster and more synchronously, before muscles grow at all.
micro_lesson.takeaway: Early strength is software updates; muscle growth is the hardware upgrade.

questions.prompt: Why does ice float on water when most solids sink in their liquids?
options: Hydrogen bonding forms an open crystal lattice less dense than liquid water
questions.explanation: As water freezes, hydrogen bonds lock molecules into a hexagonal lattice with more empty space than the liquid — about 9% less dense, so it floats. This anomaly lets lakes freeze top-down and aquatic life survive winter.

micro_lesson.title: Water's Anomaly
micro_lesson.body: Water is densest at 4°C, not at freezing. Lakes stratify: 4°C water sinks to the bottom while ice caps the surface and insulates below.
micro_lesson.takeaway: One weird molecule property underwrites every frozen lake ecosystem on Earth.

questions.prompt: Why is a diversified portfolio considered lower-risk than a single stock?
options: Uncorrelated losses offset: no single failure can sink the whole portfolio
More stocks always means more profit
Brokers charge less for many holdings
questions.explanation: Diversification spreads exposure across assets whose prices don't move together. One company can go to zero; a broad basket effectively cannot, so the portfolio's variance falls without proportionally lowering expected return.

micro_lesson.title: Diversification
micro_lesson.body: Risk has two parts: market risk (undiversifiable) and idiosyncratic risk (company-specific). Diversification erases the second nearly for free — the only free lunch in finance.
micro_lesson.takeaway: Never bet the season on one player — build a roster.
